summary: Part 4 (09:42-11:11) of the 7.0 Refund policy (Seller) video. On the Seller Performance page (Claims management tab, Refund policy section) the trainer explains the seller-side clock: the stage timeline with seller-running and Revibe-stopped colours, the per-market column charts (SA and AE · ZA), and the side drawer that lists the claims in a column with claim ID, market, days on clock, timer and stage. His example takes a claim from the AE · ZA 6d column and says to copy its claim ID into the orders app to solve it quickly. The video closes on a 'Returns Refund Policy' slide inviting KAM questions. All 13 listed frames were opened and checked. Several numbers and terms are snapshot or unclear and are flagged below.

The timer is running: hours accrue on the clock (solid blue block).
The timer is not running: hours are banked and the claim is frozen in its column until the timer restarts (light blue block).
Seller-owned stages run the clock (dark blue). Revibe-owned stages stop it (light blue). Which stages are seller-owned differs by market.
A day on a market's axis marked with a warning icon. The screen does not define it further.
Days past the market's action day, marked in red. A claim standing in one of these is one Revibe can act on.

unclear.issue: Policy-day base conflicts on screen. The methodology says '24 working hours, and only the seller's hours count'. The chart note and drawer footnote say '24 weekday hours'. Keep both as stated, and a KAM should check the exact definition before quoting it.

The meaning of '7 / 9' and '6 / 8' is not labelled on screen. The charts suggest warning and policy-applied days (SA warning 7d and 8d, policy from 9d; AE · ZA warning 6d and 7d, policy from 8d), but the text never says which number is which.
Which stage each timeline tooltip belongs to is inferred from label position only. The tooltips do not name the stage, and they hide part of the labels.

Timeline bar segments do not map cleanly to individual stage labels in the frames. Seller or Revibe ownership is not assigned per stage here. Which stages are seller-owned outside SA is not spelled out.
The stage label 'Ship back under collection' is cut off in the frame ('Ship back under collectio'), so the full wording is not confirmed on screen.
The 'orders app' is named by the trainer but not shown on screen. Which application this is cannot be confirmed from the video.
The phrase 'that we believe will {you?} better manage your claims' has an unverified word. No slide text covers it.
Claim ID letters are ambiguous in the screenshot: '4lFzRp' could be 4IFzRp, and 'EzBS80' could use an O or a 0. Do not copy these IDs from the video.
Narration words marked {or?} and {so?} in 'if it's moving {or?} not and the current stage {so?}' are low-confidence. The drawer confirms the timer and stage columns exist.
The timers are said to have begun on 03 Sep 2026, yet the clock is said to be only 5.7 policy days old. No capture date is shown on screen, so the age cannot be checked.
